Plot method for chameleon_surrogates objects

Source: R/plots.R, R/statistical_tests.R
generate_surrogates.Rd

Visualize surrogate distributions generated by generate_surrogates. For time-series surrogates, overlays density curves of individual surrogates against the original series. For scale-metrics surrogates, plots the surrogate envelope (5th-95th percentile) alongside the observed scale-dependent metrics.

Generate surrogate realizations of scale-dependent metrics or time series under specified null hypotheses. Multiple methods are available to preserve different properties of the original data.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'chameleon_surrogates'
plot(x, ...)

generate_surrogates(
  x,
  n_surrogates = 199,
  method = c("scale_shuffle", "fourier", "iaaft", "block_bootstrap"),
  block_length = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Object of class scale_metrics, object of class chameleon_analysis, numeric matrix of D and theta values by scale, or numeric vector (time series). When method = "scale_shuffle" and x is a numeric vector or a chameleon_analysis object, the scale-resolved metrics are extracted internally via chameleon_analysis, mirroring chameleon_test.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to chameleon_analysis when scale-resolved metrics must be computed from a raw time series under method = "scale_shuffle".

n_surrogates

Integer. Number of surrogates to generate (default 199).

method

Character. Surrogate generation method (see Details).

block_length

Integer. Block length for block bootstrap (default is automatically determined as n^(1/3)).

Value

A patchwork ggplot2 composition, returned invisibly.

Object of class "chameleon_surrogates": a list of surrogate realizations, each having the same structure as the input. Attributes method, n, and input_type record the generation parameters. A plot.chameleon_surrogates method is available.

Details

The surrogate distribution provides the null distribution for the chameleon test. For series-type surrogates, each density curve represents one realization of the null model; for scale-metrics surrogates, the ribbon spans the 5th-95th percentile of the null distribution across surrogates.

Available methods:

"scale_shuffle"

Randomly permute the frequency labels of the computed D(f) and theta(f) metrics. This directly tests whether metrics depend on scale by breaking the scale ordering while preserving the marginal distributions of the metrics. Primary method for testing H0.

"fourier"

Phase randomization via FFT. Preserves the power spectrum (linear autocorrelation structure) but destroys phase relationships and nonlinear structure. Tests whether observed patterns could arise from a linear Gaussian process.

"iaaft"

Iterative Amplitude Adjusted Fourier Transform. Preserves both the power spectrum and the amplitude distribution (histogram) of the original signal. More appropriate than Fourier surrogates for non-Gaussian data. Tests the null of a monotonic nonlinear transformation of a linear Gaussian process.

"block_bootstrap"

Circular block bootstrap. Preserves local temporal structure within blocks while destroying long-range dependence. Useful when local dynamics should be preserved but long-range correlations tested.

References

Theiler J, Eubank S, Longtin A, Galdrikian B, Farmer JD (1992). Testing for nonlinearity in time series: the method of surrogate data. Physica D 58:77-94. doi:10.1016/0167-2789(92)90102-S

Schreiber T, Schmitz A (1996). Improved surrogate data for nonlinearity tests. Physical Review Letters 77:635-638. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.635

See also

generate_surrogates, print.chameleon_surrogates, summary.chameleon_surrogates, chameleon_test, plot.chameleon_test.

chameleon_test for the main testing function; print.chameleon_surrogates, summary.chameleon_surrogates, plot.chameleon_surrogates for inspection of the returned surrogate ensemble.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set.seed(42)
x <- sin(seq(0, 20 * pi, length.out = 2000)) + 0.1 * rnorm(2000)
surr <- generate_surrogates(x, n_surrogates = 19)
plot(surr)
} # }

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Generate scale-shuffle surrogates from a precomputed scale_metrics object
surrogates <- generate_surrogates(scale_metrics_obj, n_surrogates = 99)

# Generate scale-shuffle surrogates directly from a time series
# (scale_metrics is computed internally via chameleon_analysis)
surrogates <- generate_surrogates(time_series, n_surrogates = 99)

# Generate IAAFT surrogates from time series
surrogates <- generate_surrogates(time_series, method = "iaaft")
} # }
